newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets close weaker as bear tone prevails.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets close weaker as bear tone prevails.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* NZ bill yields spike higher, technicals look bearish
* Concerns over weakening Kiwi depress money market
* Bonds soften after U.S. market fails to hold gains
New Zealand debt markets closed Wednesday on a distinctly bearish note, with yields sharply up across the curve and sentiment in the doldrums.

Dealers said disappointment at the U.S. market's inability to hold last night's gains had reversed early strength, and the sagging New Zealand dollar did not augur well for the short end. "Kiwi still feels heavy and tends to get sold overnight," a dealer said.
"Technicals on the 90-days, the six-months and the futures all look bearish, and the technicals on the bonds look bearish as well."
He said the market felt long and when hopes of a rally to sell into evaporated, the market was sold into the close.

The 90-day bank bill rate shot seven points higher, while bond yields rose four to five points as global markets weakened. "We have seen some offshore selling of bonds today again, it seems to be a common theme these days," said a bond trader.
"There is also a bond tender tomorrow. The last tender in December was not the most successful of tenders, so there could well be a little bit of room being made I think for the tender tomorrow."
He said the 11/06 bond was near the top of its recent range at around 7.40 percent people were a little concerned given the cloudy outlook for the U.S. market.
